messages:
Maria (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock the PRD for the serving controls feature set today. Customer asks piled up: configurable batching profiles, prefix/KV caching toggles, and a clear quantization recommendation workflow. Can we confirm acceptance criteria and edge cases?
Sam (Eng-Platform): +1. Need to decide if profiles are per-model, per-route, or per-tenant. Suggest per-route defaults with tenant overrides.
Raj (Eng-ML): Per-route default makes rollout simpler. Edge cases: variable input lengths (docs with long context) and cache correctness when prompt templates change.
Jess (SRE): Observability requirements: expose per-profile token latency pctls, cache hit/miss, and quantization mismatch rate. Also circuit-breaker when p50/99 spikes.
Alex (Design): Need a simple UI: dropdown for profile + an "advanced" panel for overrides. Show estimated token-cost delta and expected p95 change.
Maria (PM): Acceptance criteria proposal: 1) Deployable to dedicated & hosted, 2) measurable cost improvement >= 10% on sample workload OR p95 improvement >= 20% (configurable target), 3) no regressions on correctness evals (top-1 exact-match + perplexity threshold), 4) rollout canary with automatic rollback on quality regressions. Thoughts?
Raj (Eng-ML): Add: quantization recommendations should include a compatibility matrix (model -> recommended quant config) and a quick eval harness that runs a small representative eval set. We should fail-safe to FP16 when quant outcomes are bad.
Sam (Eng-Platform): Operational knobs in config (example):
```
profiles:
  default:
    batching: auto
    max_batch_size: 32
    cache: prefix
    quant: prefer-qat
  low-latency:
    batching: 0
    max_batch_size: 1
    cache: none
    quant: fp16
```
Must make sure runtime honors max_batch_size and backpressure signals.
Jess (SRE): Edge cases to include in PRD: cache invalidation when prompt templates upgrade, multi-tenant cache poisoning, and degraded hw fallback (GPU OOM -> route to smaller model). Add tests for each.
Maria (PM): For launch gates, propose: engineering sign-off, SLO dashboards in console, quantization matrix published, and runbook + rollback documented. Non-blocking: design UX polish.
Alex (Design): I'll mock the dropdown + cost tooltip by EOD. Want to confirm the two UX states: "recommended" (Auto) and "manual".
Raj (Eng-ML): On acceptance tests, define a small canonical eval set (50 prompts) and require no >2% drop in quality metrics vs baseline. Also add a reproducible seed to the harness.
Sam (Eng-Platform): Rollout plan: canary 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with automated quality checks after each step. Config exposes `canary_checks: [latency, quality, error_rate]`. deploy-bot: rollout started for canary 1% (simulated).
deploy-bot: deploy job 27381 queued, canary target=1%
Jess (SRE): Add alert thresholds: p95 latency > baseline*1.6 OR cache-miss spike > 3x baseline -> auto-rollback. Also ensure tracing tags include profile name.
Maria (PM): Great. Action items: Raj to write the RFC section on quant matrix + eval harness (due Wed), Sam to draft runtime config / canary logic (due Wed), Jess to draft SLOs/alerts and runbook (due Thu), Alex to deliver mocks (due EOD). I'll update PRD with acceptance criteria and gating items.
Sam (Eng-Platform): One more tradeoff: caching prefix means dangerous for sensitive prompts. Need a flag `cache_sensitive: false|true` and default to false for protected routes.
Raj (Eng-ML): For quantization edge case: when vocab embeddings differ between quant libs we should validate end-to-end embedding similarity before enabling. Add that to RFC.
Alex (Design): UX note: when a route is marked sensitive, hide cache toggles and show tooltip: "Caching disabled for privacy-sensitive routes."
Maria (PM): OK — I'll take this into PRD now and link the RFC draft. If anyone has objections to the acceptance thresholds let me know within 2 hours. :eyes:
Sam (Eng-Platform): No objections from infra. :thumbsup:
Jess (SRE): 👍
Raj (Eng-ML): Fine with me, will start RFC.
Alex (Design): On it.
Maria (PM): Thanks all — merging notes into PRD and tagging owners. :white_check_mark:
